subject: QuantumTech eval: provisioning plan & success criteria

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>

Subject: QuantumTech eval: provisioning plan & success criteria

Hi Aisha —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned before we kick off the trial environment: 

Summary of goals (as discussed)
- Validate Redwood inference latency & throughput characteristics for 10–100 concurrent inference sessions (peak 200 qps with batching).
- Verify model-quality parity on our 3 canonical prompts (search-rewrite, support summarization, and structured extraction) with acceptable coherence and hallucination thresholds.
- Measure cost per 1k tokens with default caching and two quantization profiles.

Success criteria (proposed)
1) Latency: median tokenize-to-first-byte <= 120ms at 50 qps sustained.
2) Quality: pass automated eval on the canonical prompts (>=90% on intent match + <=5% critical hallucination).
3) Operational: automated rotation of API keys and IP-restricted control plane access in place; SSO access for 5 pilot users.

PoC timeline (target)
- Week 0 (this week): Access provisioning, test account creation, and network allowlist.
- Week 1: Baseline runs with our reference model + telemetry collection.
- Week 2: Full eval against canonical prompts, run cost comparisons and handoff.

What we need from QuantumTech to get started
- SSO admin email(s) for invites (IdP: Okta).
- Public egress IP ranges (or the person who manages firewall rules) for allowlist.
- 2–3 sample prompt files (if you have custom prompts) and any PII/PI policy constraints.

Internal owners on our side
- Vivek Kulkarni (Solutions) — provisioning, IP allowlist, demo keys.
- Monica Patel (Customer Success) — success criteria, eval coordination, SLO checkins.
- Myself — point for sales/contract questions and timeline.

I’ll attach a short method-of-procedure (MOP) for the network steps and a CSV template for the IP column to make it easy for your infra team. Once we have the SSO admin and IP ranges I’ll have Vivek kick off provisioning.

Thanks — talk soon,

Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.inference
(650) 555-0192

Hi Karthik —

Thanks for the clear summary — that matches our notes. We can move fast on this. A couple quick items from our side: 

1) SSO: Okta admin is me (aisha.bennett@quantumtech.io) — please send the invite to that address. We’ll add the pilot user list after the invite is accepted.
2) IPs: attaching the template you sent with our public egress ranges filled (see network-ip-template.csv). There are three NAT egress ranges: 34.54.12.0/24, 34.55.0.0/16, and 35.12.100.0/24.
3) API keys: is there an option for short-lived API keys or token rotation during the trial? We’d prefer rotating creds every 24 hours for the test harness.

Tentative timeline: we can complete allowlist & SSO invite by EOD Wed (Mar 3). If so, we’re good to start baseline runs Thurs (Mar 4).

I attached the CSV. Let us know if you need anything else from infra.

Best,
Aisha
Director, Platform Engineering
QuantumTech

Hi Aisha —

Thanks for the quick turn on the IPs and for confirming you’ll be the Okta admin. I’ll start the provisioning checklist tomorrow. A few notes and an outline of what we’ll do on our side: 

Provisioning MOP (high level)
- Create service account and short-lived API key (we can issue a key that rotates via our control plane; for a 24-hour rotation we’ll provide a script and token TTL controls).
- Add the three egress ranges you provided to the control plane allowlist.
- Invite SSO admin (you) and create 5 pilot user slots.
- Wire telemetry: we’ll configure a temporary debug level (no PII capture) and open a metrics stream to your SRE inbox.

Owners and ETA
- Today/Tomorrow: MOP walkthrough and invite (me).
- By Wed EOD (Mar 3): allowlist added and Okta invite sent (depends on you accepting the invite).
- Thurs (Mar 4): baseline runs begin; Monica will coordinate the canonical prompt runs.

I’ve attached our redwood-eval-mop.pdf (step-by-step checklist). A couple clarifying questions for you: 
- Can you confirm if any of the egress ranges are NATed behind additional customer firewalls? If so, we’ll need a contact for that team.
- For API rotation, do you have an existing automation we should integrate with (e.g., HashiCorp Vault)? If yes, please share the integration contact or a brief note.

We’ll keep the trial credentials isolated to a dedicated org and purge keys after the eval window.

Cheers,
Vivek Kulkarni
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.inference
